sections.introduction: The pie charts compare the main reasons why people migrated to and from the UK in 2007.
sections.overview: Overall, having a definite job was the primary reason for both immigration and emigration. In addition, formal study accounted for a significantly higher percentage among immigrants than emigrants, whereas looking for work was more common for those leaving the UK.
sections.body1: Regarding immigration, the proportion of people moving to the UK for a definite job was highest, at 30%, followed by formal study (26%). In contrast, accompanying or joining family members stood at 15%, while the figure for looking for work was slightly lower, at 12%. Meanwhile, other reasons and no reason stated accounted for far less of the total, at 11% and 6% respectively.
sections.body2: Looking at emigration, the percentage of people leaving for a definite job (29%) far exceeded that of looking for work and formal study, with respective figures being 22% and 4%. About 18% of emigrants left without stating a reason, compared to 14% for other reasons and 13% for accompanying or joining family. Notably, the proportion of immigrants coming to the UK for formal study was more than six times as high as that of emigrants leaving for the same purpose.

sections.introduction: The diagram describes the process of recycling organic waste to produce fertiliser, also known as compost.
sections.overview: Overall, the process comprises five main steps, beginning with the preparation of a plastic container and ending with the application of the finished compost in the garden.
sections.body1: At the beginning of the process, a plastic container with a volume of two cubic metres is prepared, with holes on its sides to allow air circulation. Next, various organic materials are placed inside the container in layers. A 15-centimetre layer of food is added at the bottom, which is followed by a 15-centimetre layer of grass, a layer of newspaper, and other organic waste on top. Once these ingredients are assembled, nitrogen and a small amount of hot water are poured into the mixture to accelerate the decomposition process.
sections.body2: The process continues with sealing the container using a lid. During this stage, heat is generated inside the container, after which the organic waste is left to ferment over a period of six months. Finally, at the final stage of the process, the organic waste is fully converted into compost, which can then be used to nourish plants in the garden.

sections.introduction: The diagram describes the process of manufacturing carbonated drinks through five distinct stages.
sections.overview: Overall, the process comprises five main stages, beginning with water cleaning and ending with the packaging and transportation of the finished products to supermarkets.
sections.body1: At the beginning of the process, raw water is passed through a filter and a water softener before being treated with chemicals to remove impurities. Once the water is cleaned, it is pumped into electric heaters, which is followed by passing through a cooling pipe. Subsequently, carbon dioxide is added to the water in order to produce carbonated water.
sections.body2: The process continues with the carbonated water being transferred to a mixing tank, where colouring, syrup, and flavouring are added. After the mixture is thoroughly combined, it goes through a filter once again before being filled into bottles or cans. Finally, at the final stage of the process, the packaged drinks are placed into cardboard boxes, after which they are loaded onto trucks and delivered to supermarkets.

sections.introduction: The diagram describes the life cycle of a salmon from the egg stage to an adult fish.
sections.overview: Overall, the process is a continuous cyclical cycle comprising several distinct stages, which take place in three main environments: rivers, estuaries, and the ocean.
sections.body1: At the beginning of the cycle, adult salmon lay eggs in the river, after which the eggs undergo an incubation period. Once the eggs hatch, young salmon emerge and enter the freshwater rearing stage, where they stay and grow for a period of time. Subsequently, these small fish migrate downstream towards the estuary, at which point they adapt to the brackish water during the estuary rearing phase.
sections.body2: The process continues with the fish migrating further out into the open ocean.
